q: What is the first useful response to a user who reports suspicious mail?
options: Acknowledge receipt and give a trusted follow-up route
Ask the user to reply to the suspicious sender for confirmation
Promise that the message is harmless because it was reported
Require the user to reopen the link before receiving a case number
explanation: A clear acknowledgment keeps the user informed and preserves evidence.

q: A reporter says the email was opened. What should the analyst clarify?
options: Whether they want the case assigned to the department manager
Whether the mail system has a title that can be read aloud
Whether the reported file name can be replaced by the ticket number
Whether they viewed the message or opened its file
explanation: The word opened may refer to materially different activity.

q: A user volunteers their actual password during intake. What is the right action?
options: Ask the user to enter the password verbatim in the ticket
Use the value to calculate an identifier for sharing with colleagues
Stop secret collection and route the reported exposure
Replace the value with a question about verifying it on the original page
explanation: Capture the kind of exposure and involve the authorised identity owner.

q: Which report route best supports preserving original mail?
options: An ordinary forward to an external address suggested in the message
The organisation's supported report button or authorised export
A call in which the analyst guesses every header field
A screenshot attached after the original message is deleted
explanation: A supported route can preserve the message structure and essential metadata.

q: Two recipients report copies of one suspected campaign. One entered credentials. What is the right record?
options: Group related records and keep each exposure separately
Merge the submissions and keep only the first employee's actions
Open one undifferentiated credential incident for every possible recipient
Treat duplicate reports as noise after recording the shared subject
explanation: Campaign linkage does not erase individual evidence or ownership.

q: What distinguishes a reported time from a ticket-created time?
options: The reported time automatically determines when the case system stored the record
The ticket's creation time proves exactly when the user clicked
The two time fields should be merged whenever either is approximate
The reported time describes the event as recalled
explanation: The source and meaning of each time matter to later investigation.

q: An employee reports approving an unexpected sign-in prompt. What should happen before attachment classification finishes?
options: Wait for the mail team to classify all matching attachments first
Request the employee's security code to reproduce the approval
Escalate to the identity owner with the action and time
Use the sender's contact details to confirm the prompt was expected
explanation: A reported approval can warrant prompt response independent of message classification.

q: What do two reports with the same subject establish?
options: That the exact same raw message reached both recipients
A possible relationship that needs corroboration
That both recipient devices opened the same attachment
That one employee's account sent every related copy
explanation: Common subject lines provide a lead rather than establishing identity.

q: A gateway saw automated previews but a user also reports clicking. What should the analyst do?
options: Keep both records and seek corroborating device evidence
Discard the user's statement because automated traffic is present
Count the previews as separate confirmations of employee clicks
Replace the reporter's approximate time with the first preview timestamp
explanation: Service activity does not cancel or independently validate a human report.

q: What should an acknowledgment ask the reporter to avoid?
options: Using any recognised reporting channels for follow-up
Keeping a note of what they did and when it happened
Waiting for direction from an authorised responder
Reopening the suspicious content while the case is reviewed
explanation: Avoiding renewed interaction protects both the employee and the evidence.

q: The message asks a user to call a number to contact IT. Which route should the SOC recommend?
options: The message number after checking its area code matches local support
The first number shown in the employee's recent call list
The independently published IT or incident desk contact
The sender's mobile number as long as another employee can dial it
explanation: A known route avoids relying on a potentially misleading contact.

q: Which statement belongs in the reported-action field?
options: The SOC proves compromise because the employee seemed anxious
The employee reports clicking at approximately 08:06 UTC
The gateway logged a preview, so the employee must have approved a prompt
A colleague expects the invoice is fake, based only on its font
explanation: The field records what the reporter said and its certainty.

q: A user initiated a payment and no unusual process was observed. What takes priority?
options: Contact the authorised Finance and incident owners promptly
Wait until endpoint monitoring detects a suspicious application
Treat absence of an endpoint signal as proof of no business impact
Direct the mail team to issue a company-wide technical attribution
explanation: Financial consequences can be urgent without an observed malware event.

q: A private phone screenshot includes unrelated personal notifications. What is the appropriate intake choice?
options: Upload the full screenshot to the ticket as the default response
Ask for every conversation from the same personal phone
Discard the report entirely because it came from a non-work device
Seek necessary fields through the approved collection route
explanation: Collect the information the case needs while respecting the approved scope.

q: Which question is best in the first intake conversation?
options: Why did you fail to identify the phishing message?
Which malware family owned the sender's suspicious account?
What did you see and do next?
How can you guarantee that nothing compromised your device?
explanation: Neutral questions elicit actionable observations without asking for analysis.

q: An account may be under investigation. How should follow-up identity be verified?
options: Rely on replies from the mailbox through which the suspicious activity arrived
Use an approved independent channel and record the route
Assume the person using the displayed account name is always authorised
Ask the reporter to return to the same link to resume the conversation
explanation: A separate channel lowers dependence on a potentially affected account.

q: What information helps a reviewer improve the reporting process?
options: Acknowledgment and handoff times with defined endpoints
The identity of every employee presented in an unrestricted report
The volume of deleted mail without any indication of reporting channel
A count of screenshots received without context or comparison
explanation: Defined timings help identify delays and improve routing.

q: A later technical log refines a reporter's approximate time. How should the case be updated?
options: Overwrite the person's statement with the technical record everywhere
Remove the technical record because it does not exactly match the estimate
Round both timestamps to the ticket date and omit how they were obtained
Record both times with their sources and explain the refinement
explanation: Source-labeled entries help reviewers follow the change in confidence.

q: Which factor can improve accessibility of a reporting route?
options: Require a desktop-only plugin as the sole reporting route
Hide instructions until an employee uses the report button
Offer keyboard-accessible and supported fallback channels
Require copying the full original into every support channel
explanation: A route should be available to staff in the ways they work.

q: A reported call shows a familiar number in caller ID. What can be recorded?
options: The identity of the caller as verified by the displayed number
The displayed number, reported context and actions
The original network route taken by the call without provider records
A verified payment request because the number looked familiar
explanation: Caller ID is an observation and does not establish who called.

q: What should be retained when linking duplicate reports?
options: The individual report sources, times and exposure details
Only the combined ticket number for all reported events
Only the last recorded subject from the mail gateway
The action of the person who made the earliest report
explanation: Individual exposure can differ across otherwise related deliveries.

q: A supported route cannot preserve the original on mobile. What should the SOC do?
options: Reject the report until the employee activates every suspicious object again
Treat the mobile screenshot as a full RFC message export
Require the employee to install an unrelated unapproved analysis tool
Accept the initial report and arrange authorised acquisition
explanation: Start protective response while documenting the acquisition limitation.

q: An employee has forgotten the time of a possible interaction. What helps later scoping?
options: Use the ticket creation time and present it as the verified click time
Remove the interaction field until the employee supplies an exact second
Record an approximate interval and relevant work context
Use the first available gateway timestamp regardless of the reported activity
explanation: A bounded estimate is clearer than a precise but unsupported value.

q: What is the purpose of a closure update to a reporter?
options: Reveal the identities of all other reporters who received the message
State any remaining action and share permitted findings
Repeat the suspicious content and provide its original active links
Publish the full ongoing incident timeline without access restrictions
explanation: A brief update supports trust and gives an action if needed.

q: How should a report with no interaction and a suspicious original be handled?
options: Preserve it and assess delivery and classification
Ignore it because individual compromise has not been demonstrated
Automatically disable every account listed in the message body
Require the reporter to retrieve additional examples by following the link
explanation: The original can reveal additional exposure even without interaction.
